citation.title: Deep learning-based topology optimization design method for bridge structures guided by aesthetics
citation.authors: C. Xiang, A. R. Chen, Y. Ning, D. L. Wang
citation.version_coded: open-access version of record reproduced on ResearchGate

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The proposed network is said to generate pylon designs quickly, with mechanical and aesthetic merit, but no tested comparison with classical optimization is presented.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No paired classical and learned runtimes are printed.
claim.alternatives: Section 3 says offline sample requirements are lower than for earlier learned methods.

baseline.classical_method: Section 3: topology optimization method of Andreassen et al. (2011) used to generate training examples
baseline.problem_size: Section 3: pylon height 256 and width 64-128 in image coordinates
baseline.data_generation_cost: Section 3: 102 portal-type and 306 portal-truss examples generated by classical topology optimization; computational cost not stated
baseline.quality_metric: Section 4: selected visual designs and aesthetic network output

R1.evidence: Section 3-4: no optimization-level classical comparison; full-text excluded.

R2.evidence: Section 3-4: no optimization-level classical comparison; full-text excluded.

R3.evidence: Section 3-4: no optimization-level classical comparison; full-text excluded.

R4.evidence: Section 3-4: no optimization-level classical comparison; full-text excluded.

reporting.n_test_cases: Section 3: selected pylon design examples; number of generated test designs not stated

notes: The paper uses classical topology optimization to generate training examples (section 3), but its evaluation presents selected learned pylon designs and aesthetic scores without a measured or cited comparative classical result.
